::: {.callout-note title="Editable submission handout"}
[Open the Linux Mint Installation Digital Submission Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/120xWMTjO7YDA8XPMSy9Cy5rLjfBZixSiIRb3AvZQn_w/edit?usp=drivesdk). Attach it in Google Classroom and make a copy for each student when you create the assignment.

Related class materials: [installation notes](install-linux-mint.qmd), [Linux unit overview](index.qmd), and [Linux Start Here slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1V9VzFkTGhEyKs5TszsuZV96xya5k-zvfEx8qGKjgbzM/edit).
:::

## Learning goal

By the end of this submission:

- I will be able to show that Linux Mint works on my assigned computer.
- I will be able to explain what I noticed during the installation.

This is important because it enables me to show clear evidence of my work and explain what I learned.

::: {.callout-important title="What to submit"}
Submit **one Google Doc** in Google Classroom.

Name it: `Linux Mint Installation - First name - Computer name`

Example: `Linux Mint Installation - Sam - min-tej-14`

Do not submit separate screenshots. Insert them into the Google Doc.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Keep private information private"}
Do not put a password, Wi-Fi password, student number, access token, or other private information in your Google Doc or screenshots.
:::

## Build your Google Doc

1. Open the Linux Mint installation assignment in Google Classroom.
2. Create or attach **one Google Doc**.
3. Give the file the required name.
4. Add the headings shown below.
5. Answer every required prompt.
6. Insert your screenshot directly below the matching prompt.

## Copy these headings and prompts

### Installation result

**Computer name:**
Write the unique computer name you used.

**Did the TEJ Notes website load?**
Write Yes or No. If it did not load, explain what happened.

**Software installed:**
Write the exact name of the school-appropriate game or application you installed.

**What does the software do?**
Explain it in one or two sentences.

**Finished desktop:**
Insert **one screenshot** that shows the installed Linux Mint desktop. Make sure the screenshot does not show private information.

### What I noticed

Answer each question in one or two complete sentences.

1. What is one thing you like about Linux Mint?
2. What is one thing you do not like or do not understand yet?
3. What is one difference you noticed between Linux Mint and Windows?
4. What would you like to learn next?

### Problem solving

**What problem did you solve?**
Describe one problem and what you did to solve it.

If nothing went wrong, describe one installation choice that you checked carefully and explain why it mattered.

## Above and beyond

This section is optional, but the heading must be in your Google Doc.

If you completed only the required work, write: `I completed the required work.`

If you went further, answer the questions that apply:

- What did you do beyond the required work?
- What did you investigate, test, customize, or create?
- What extra problem did you solve?
- What evidence can you show?
- What would you explore next if you had more time?

You may include one extra screenshot below this section.

## Before you turn it in

- [ ] I attached **one Google Doc**.
- [ ] My file name follows the required pattern.
- [ ] I answered every required prompt.
- [ ] I inserted one readable desktop screenshot.
- [ ] My document contains no passwords or private information.
- [ ] I included the **Above and beyond** heading.
- [ ] I selected **Turn in** in Google Classroom.

## Extend your learning

- Return to the [Linux Mint installation notes](install-linux-mint.qmd) or review the [Linux Start Here class slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1V9VzFkTGhEyKs5TszsuZV96xya5k-zvfEx8qGKjgbzM/edit).
- Visit the [Linux Mint documentation](https://linuxmint.com/documentation.php) to find official user guides for the desktop and system tools.
- Explore the school-appropriate [Learn Linux TV YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@LearnLinuxTV) for beginner Linux demonstrations. Choose a beginner video and write down one new idea.
- Try the [Ubuntu command-line tutorial](https://documentation.ubuntu.com/desktop/en/latest/tutorial/the-linux-command-line-for-beginners/) when you are ready to explore beyond the desktop.

## Review

You created one clear Google Doc, recorded the installation result, explained what you noticed, and showed evidence that Linux Mint works.

## Reflect on your learning

1. Which part of your Google Doc gives the clearest evidence that the installation worked?
2. What would make your next technical submission clearer?
